epic.name: Light and Dark Themes
unverifiedAssumptions: With JavaScript disabled the app renders in LIGHT, because the pre-paint script is the only thing that can know the right theme and the server renders no theme class at all. Reasonable now that light is a first-class theme, but it is an interpretation of "dark remains the default look" — worth a nod.

A theme chosen in one tab does not update another already-open tab until it reloads; the choice is read once per document load. No acceptance criterion covers cross-tab behaviour, so it was left out rather than guessed at.

Look at the plain outlined buttons in BOTH themes - Retry, Cancel, Edit animal. They are filled with the same colour as the page behind them, so only a very faint hairline says where the button is (1.38:1 in light, 1.24:1 in dark, against a 3:1 standard). It is equally faint in dark - slightly worse there - so light did not break it, and the hairline comes from a shared colour used by every outlined button. Changing it is a design decision for you, not a light-only patch.

The automated accessibility scan walks five normal screens. It does NOT cover the loading / nothing-here-yet / no-matches / failed-to-load / not-found / refused-save states, which is exactly what story 5 was about. Those were checked by measurement and by eye this once, but a future colour regression in one of them would only be caught by eye.
